description: We are a team of young innovators passionate about space, science, technology, and game development. We aim to create an interactive earth trend detection system that shows the twelve Earth science variables and help users to understand the changing Earth. We also want to protect by helping scientists and communities understand the risks , predict potential risks and make informed decisions.
summary: Earth System Trend Detective is a free, no-install web tool that helps anyone investigate how the Earth is changing. Users choose from twelve demo Earth science variables such as temperature, CO₂, sea ice, sea level, ocean heat, snow cover and more. Set a time window, and instantly see what changed, how fast, where the change is strongest, and whether the trend is statistically significant. The app combines interactive charts, an illustrative 5° map, latitude profiles, plain-language summaries and three statistical methods (OLS trend, Mann–Kendall test and Sen's slope). A one-click loader adds the exact NASA GISTEMP v4 record for authoritative analysis, while every other dataset is clearly labelled as demo data. A Simple view hides technical tables for first-time visitors, and a Share button preserves the selected variable and years in the URL. Built with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, it runs offline, requires no account, and was independently verified against SciPy. It turns a complex climate record into evidence the public can understand. The Earth Trend Detection can help protect our earth by identifying and monitoring the enviromental changes. By analysing NASA satellite date , it helps scientists and communities understand the risks, predict potential risks and make informed decisions.
details:
Earth System Trend Detective is an interactive web-based platform designed to help users explore and understand changes in Earth's climate and environmental systems. It focuses on four major indicators: global temperature, Arctic sea ice, global sea level, and atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO₂).

The application allows users to explore historical data through interactive graphs, compare trends, and perform statistical analysis. It follows four investigation stages: Select, Quantify, Locate, and Verify.

Developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, the platform aims to make complex scientific data easier to understand and accessible to everyone. Its main impact is to increase climate awareness, encourage scientific thinking, and support evidence-based environmental decisions.

A Simple view hides technical tables for first-time visitors, and a Share button preserves the selected variable and years in the URL. Built with plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, it runs offline, requires no account, and was independently verified against SciPy.

The project's uniqueness lies in its detective-style approach, allowing users to investigate environmental changes rather than simply viewing graphs. During development, we considered data reliability, scientific accuracy, accessibility, and user-friendly design.
